facts.claim: The position must be that of an ADDED (+) line.
facts.verified: partial: a review comment/suggestion can target any line in the diff; suggestions are normally placed on the RIGHT side (added or unchanged context lines); deleted (LEFT) lines are also commentable (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments#create-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request side LEFT/RIGHT)

facts.claim: To have a suggestion replace several lines, the comment must span them (start_line+line, or the UI range selection); a suggestion on a single-line comment replaces only that line.
facts.verified: partial: skill never mentions start_line/start_side and says 'Include surrounding lines for context (GitHub shows ~3 lines of context)'; including unchanged neighbouring lines inside a single-line suggestion duplicates them on apply. Multi-line ranges per https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments#create-a-review-comment-for-a-pull-request (start_line/start_side) and commenting-on-a-pull-request docs

facts.claim: Build the review JSON with an unquoted heredoc (`<<JSON`, so $COMMIT_SHA expands) using `\\n` for newlines and `\`\`\`` for fences; escape quotes, backticks and newlines in JSON.
facts.verified: WRONG: JSON needs \n, \" and \\ escaped but backticks need NO JSON escaping. In the Approach 1 example, `\\\`` inside the unquoted heredoc becomes `\`` in the file, an invalid JSON escape — reproduced locally: `jq` fails 'Invalid escape' on the 'Add an \\\`ok\\\` flag' body; the Quick Start template (no \\\` sequences) produces valid JSON. Safer: build the payload with `jq -n --arg`
facts.quiz: excluded: claim is wrong; fix in skill first

facts.claim: Accepting a suggestion creates a commit on the PR branch with the suggester as co-author; the author can 'Commit suggestion' individually or 'Add suggestion to batch' then 'Commit suggestions' from the Files changed tab.
facts.verified: verified: https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/incorporating-feedback-in-your-pull-request ('Each person who suggested a change included in the commit will be a co-author'; Commit suggestion / Add suggestion to batch / Commit suggestions); applying requires write access (or maintainer edits on a fork)

facts.claim: Putting multiple suggestions in one review enables batch application.
facts.verified: partial: batching works across any suggestions on the PR regardless of which review they came from (https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/reviewing-changes-in-pull-requests/incorporating-feedback-in-your-pull-request); one review mainly means one notification

facts.claim: 'Invalid commit_id' comes from using an old commit SHA; get the current HEAD SHA before creating the review.
facts.verified: partial: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews#create-a-review-for-a-pull-request says an older SHA 'may render your review comment outdated if a subsequent commit modifies the line'; it is not itself rejected — 'commit_id' errors arise when the SHA isn't part of the PR

facts.claim: A suggestion can't be applied after a merge conflict or branch update; the author must update the branch first.
facts.verified: partial: GitHub disables applying suggestions on outdated comments (the line changed since) or on closed/merged PRs; not specifically a 'merge conflict' rule — unverified detail

facts.claim: Suggestions work in the GitHub mobile app.
facts.verified: unverified

facts.claim: Post summary comments with `gh pr comment <N> --repo owner/repo --body "..."` (use a quoted heredoc `$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF)` for multi-line bodies).
facts.verified: verified: `gh pr comment --help` (--body/-b, --repo/-R)

facts.claim: `gh pr review` posts a review with --approve / --request-changes / --comment and a body.
facts.verified: verified: `gh pr review --help` (-a, -r, -c, -b/--body, -F/--body-file); note gh pr review cannot attach inline comments/suggestions, which need gh api

facts.claim: Fix commits: get headRefName/headRepositoryOwner via gh pr view --json, `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head:pr-<N>`, check out, fix, `npm run lint`, commit, then `git push origin pr-<N>:$BRANCH` and explain the fixes in a PR comment.
facts.verified: partial: refs/pull/<N>/head fetch is valid and the JSON fields exist (`gh pr view --help`), but `git push origin ...` only works when the head branch is in the base repo; for fork PRs push to the fork (headRepository) — the computed REPO_OWNER is never used. `gh pr checkout <N>` handles both

facts.claim: Pushing fix commits needs write access; for forks, the author must have enabled maintainer edits ('usually default for same-org PRs').
facts.verified: partial: 'Allow edits from maintainers' applies only to PRs from forks in personal accounts (https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/allowing-changes-to-a-pull-request-branch-created-from-a-fork); same-repo/same-org branches need only write access

facts.claim: Fix-commit message format: `fix: <short description>`, details, list of changes, and 'Addresses review feedback: <link>'.
facts.verified: n/a: convention
